subject: Order Form SLA — credit tolerance & maintenance blackout proposal
messages:
From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@kestrel.io>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@kestrel.io
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — uptime & maintenance

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is enthusiastic about Redwood but our legal and SRE teams pushed back on a few SLA items in the draft Order Form, specifically:

- 99.95% uptime appears optimistic for our EU-heavy traffic; we need clarity on measurement windows and whether partial-region events are prorated.
- Service credit cap of 30% over a quarter is higher than our procurement policy allows. Can we agree to a per-incidence cap and an annual maximum?
- Maintenance windows: Kestrel requires two weekly blackouts (Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC) for our compliance testing; we need guaranteed blackout protection during those times or a 72hr notice and makegood.
- Response SLAs for P1/P2 incidents: our SOC expects a 15-minute initial response for P1s.

I attached our redlines (Kestrel_OrderForm_SLA_redlines_v1.docx). Legal is on copy — if you can propose concrete countertext for each bullet we can iterate.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Porter
Head of Cloud Ops, Kestrel Cloud Solutions

Attachment: Kestrel_OrderForm_SLA_redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime & maintenance

Thanks Elaine — appreciate the clear ask. Looping in Marcus (ops), Connor (support), and Kimberly (legal) to propose firm language.

Quick notes from my side:
- Measurement: we measure uptime per-account, per-region, with a rolling 30-day window; credits are prorated by affected region unless customer elects global measurement for a fee. Happy to put the exact clause in the Order Form.
- Credit cap: we can propose a per-incident cap (e.g., up to 10% of monthly recurring charges per incident) and an annual cap at 50% of MRC — but need legal to confirm.
- Maintenance blackouts: we don't currently guarantee blackout protection (we maintain a flexible maintenance cadence across fleet). We can discuss either dedicated blackout carveouts for a reserved Dedicated pool or a 72hr notice + makegood.
- P1 response: 15-minute SLA for initial acknowledgment is aggressive for hosted tiers; we can commit to 30 minutes on hosted, 15 min on Dedicated with an escalation path.

Marcus / Connor / Kimberly — can each propose tight redline text for the docx attached? I'll consolidate and send back to Elaine and legal.

-Rafael
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime & maintenance

Rafael — jumping in from an ops angle. Draft language suggestions below (feel free to copy into Order Form):

1) Uptime measurement
"Availability" means the percentage of successful request responses to Redwood-managed inference endpoints measured on a per-region basis over a rolling 30-day window. An "affected region" is a geographic region (e.g., us-west-2, eu-west-1) where 50% or more of customer requests failed due to Redwood service unavailability. Customer may elect, for an additional fee, to have Availability measured on a global basis; otherwise credits are applied only to impacted region billing.

2) Service credits / caps
Service Credit per incident = min(10% of monthly recurring charges (MRC), cost of affected capacity). Annual cap on credits = 50% of MRC. Credits issued only after documented root-cause analysis and validation by Redwood operations; suspected customer misconfig/third-party infra exclusions apply.

3) Maintenance blackout carveout
Customer may nominate up to two weekly blackout windows (maximum 4 hours each) during which Redwood will not schedule non-emergency maintenance for hosted resources supported by the Order Form. For Dedicated deployments, Redwood will implement blackout windows at the cluster/pool level. If Redwood must perform emergency maintenance during a nominated blackout, Redwood will provide a makegood consisting of a partial credit equal to 5% of monthly bill for the affected region in addition to operational remediation steps.

4) P1 response
Initial response defined as creation of a dedicated incident channel and acknowledgment of receipt. Hosted tier: 30 minutes; Dedicated tier: 15 minutes. Full remediation timelines remain subject to severity and customer-provided runbooks.

I want to avoid opening an unlimited blackout guarantee — ops overhead skyrockets. Connor, please add anything on proof/callout for RCA gating.

—Marcus
Principal Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: connor.obrien@redwood.ai <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Marcus — a couple of operational clarifications to tighten the redline text:

- RCA gating: credits should require a post-incident RCA within 14 calendar days and acceptance of the RCA by customer. If a customer disputes the RCA, credits are paused until resolution.
- Partial-region definition: add an example to avoid disagreement (e.g., regional routing failure vs single-AZ outage).
- Emergency maintenance definition: limit to events where continuing service would result in immediate data loss or regulatory risk; planned security patches should not be classified as emergency.

I'll mock a short example clause and attach the maintenance blackout proposal PDF for Kestrel's reviewers.

Connor
Senior Support Lead
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime & maintenance

Hi Elaine — legal here. I've reviewed Marcus and Connor's operational text and propose contract-ready redline snippets below. Two items for negotiation: the annual credit cap and the blackout makegood definition.

Proposed contract language (to insert into Order Form):
1) Availability and measurement: [insert Marcus text]. Definitions and measurement methods are final and binding; measurement data will be shared in a customer portal.
2) Credits: "Customer will be eligible for Service Credits when Availability falls below the thresholds set forth below. Service Credits are calculated as a percentage of applicable monthly fees for the impacted region and shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for service unavailability. For each incident, the maximum Service Credit shall not exceed 10% of the monthly fees applicable to the impacted region. The aggregate Service Credit for all incidents in a 12-month period shall not exceed 50% of the Annual Recurring Charges (ARC) attributable to the impacted region."
3) Blackout windows: "Customer may nominate up to two (2) recurring weekly blackout windows of up to four (4) hours each. Redwood will not schedule non-emergency maintenance during nominated blackout windows on resources exclusively committed to Customer. If Redwood performs emergency maintenance during a nominated blackout window, Redwood will: (a) notify Customer within 2 hours, and (b) issue a one-time makegood credit equal to 5% of the monthly fees for the impacted region, provided that Customer accepts Redwood's RCA within fourteen (14) days. Emergency maintenance is limited to actions necessary to prevent imminent data loss, security breaches, or material regulatory non-compliance."

Suggested compromise on credit cap: we can offer a reduction of the annual aggregate cap from 50% of ARC to 40% if Kestrel accepts a global-measurement opt-in fee and a 72-hour advance notice clause for non-emergency major upgrades.

Please confirm which items are deal-breakers; happy to iterate quickly.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@kestrel.io>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, marcuss.lin@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime & maintenance

Kimberly / Rafael — thanks for the fast turnaround and pragmatic options. A few quick responses from Kestrel:

- The 10% per-incident cap with a 40% annual cap (in exchange for global measurement) is acceptable to procurement. We'll need that option spelled out in the Order Form and an explicit opt-in checkbox on the portal/account settings.
- Blackout windows: we can accept the emergency carve definition but need the makegood credit to be 7% for the first occurrence in a contract year and 10% for subsequent occurrences — our compliance team needs stronger deterrence.
- P1 response: Kestrel insists on a 15-minute acknowledgment across both Hosted and Dedicated for the first 6 months of the contract as a runway; after 6 months, this reverts to the standard Hosted/Dedicated split.

Legal is okay to proceed if you can put the proposed redlines into a clean Order Form and share a DocuSign link. I'll also get procurement to confirm the opt-in fee amount and we can close next week.

Elaine

- Rafael: prepare a clean Order Form with the negotiated text (include both the 40% annual cap opt-in path and the standard 50% cap) and generate DocuSign.

- Kimberly: prepare the legal clause with the graduated blackout makegood (7% then 10%) and the opt-in mechanics.

I'll follow up once procurement confirms the opt-in fee.

Best,
